message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today National Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). Known for his versatility, athleticism, court vision, and leadership, he has been selected to numerous All‑NBA teams and has represented the United States in international competition, winning gold medals at the 2008, 2012, and 2016 Olympics.

Beyond the court, LeBron is also a philanthropist, entrepreneur, and media personality. He founded the LeBron James Family Foundation, which focuses on education initiatives such as the I Promise School in Akron. He has produced films and television shows through his company SpringHill Entertainment and has been involved in various business ventures, including ownership stakes in sports teams and partnerships with major brands.
